title: Within-case CCZ classification of relative-trace APN functions
summary: Classify CCZ equivalence within cases (i), (ii), (iii), and (v) of the relative-trace APN construction solely by the index parameter.

formal_statement.body: Let $f_{i,s,a,b,c}$ and $f_{\ell,t,u,v,k}$ be source-admissible APN functions belonging to the same one of cases (i), (ii), (iii), or (v) of Theorem 2. Prove that they are CCZ-equivalent if and only if $i=\ell$, independently of the admissible coefficients, or give a counterexample to either direction.

scope.domain: CCZ-equivalence classes of the source's relative-trace quadratic APN functions
assumptions: $f_{i,s,a,b,c}(x)=a\operatorname{Tr}_m^n(bx^{2^i+1})+a^q\operatorname{Tr}_m^n(cx^{2^s+1})$ is an APN instance in the indicated case of source Theorem 2
scope.unresolved_remainder: Published later work proves coefficient-independent EA, hence CCZ, equivalence only for the case-(i), $i=1$, $3\nmid m$ subfamily. The biconditional across all admissible indices and coefficients in cases (i), (ii), (iii), and (v) remains unresolved.

citations.label: Shi--Peng--Zheng--Lu, equivalence of APN quadrinomials and power functions
citations.locator: Introduction, Theorems 2 and 4, and conclusion, pp. 353, 356--358, and 361--362

progress.summary: Assertion 1 conjectures that, within each of cases (i), (ii), (iii), and (v), CCZ equivalence is determined exactly by equality of the index.
Later published work proves coefficient-independent EA equivalence for the strict case-(i), $i=1$, $3\nmid m$ subfamily, leaving all other cases and the distinct-index direction open.
